newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA START AS FAVOURITES IN TRIANGULAR SERIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA START AS FAVOURITES IN TRIANGULAR SERIES.

text.p: Australia may lament the
absence of Shane Warne and India may worry about the batting
form of new captain Sachin Tendulkar, leaving South Africa as
favourites to win the triangular one-day cricket series which
begins on Thursday.
South Africa have no title wins on the sub-continent but go
into the three-leg round-robin preliminary matches in confident
form after a morale-boosing title win in the four-nation
tournament in Kenya.
Leg-spinner Shane Warne pulled out of the tour with an
injury and host nation India hope that his absence will help
them.
"His absence will be detrimental to Australian prospects and
could have an adverse affect on the team's performance,"
Tendulkar said on Wednesday in Hyderabad, where India play South
Africa in a day-night tie on Thursday.
South African captain Hansie Cronje believes Tendulkar has
revitalised the Indian side, despite failing with the bat in the
one-off test against Australia in New Delhi last week.
"India seem to be doing rather well under new skipper Sachin
Tendulkar whose exuberance appears to have rubbed off on the
squad," Cronje said.
India won the test, Tendulkar's first as captain but the
player himself made only 10 in the first innings and was out for
nought in the second.
The 23-year-old captain has said he will no longer open the
innings with Nayan Mongia in one-day matches.
Tendulkar's tenure as skipper in one-day matches began with
setbacks in the four-nation tournament in Sri Lanka and the
Sahara Cup series against Pakistan in Canada.
"Tendulkar has been under pressure to perform miracles,"
former Indian captain Sunil Gavaskar wrote in a newspaper column
this week.
South Africa will be hoping to make up for their
disappointment in the World Cup on the subcontinent earlier this
year, when their batsmen were considered to have thrown away a
winnable quarter-final against West Indies.
Australian coach Geoff Marsh said last week that bowling on
the slowish Indian pitches was a big challenge but his bowlers
had the ability to adapt.
Tendulkar said there was nothing wrong in playing on wickets
which helped Indian spinners. "Every nation prepares wickets to
back its own strengths," he said.
The final of the triangular series for the Titan Cup is
scheduled to be played in Bombay on November 6.
